title: 6.11.10 Challenges: Make it yours
description: Your Star catch has sound, music and saved options. Add one sound rule of your own: a streak that climbs, a chime that comes from where you caught it, or chords cut from one file. Pick one; add an idea of your own on top if you like.

steps.title: Pick a sound rule and add it
hints: Whatever you pick, play a whole game and press R at the end: the title's tune should still come back.
Challenge 3: `const names = ['one', 'two', 'three', 'four'];` then `const pick = floor(random(names.length));` then `notes.play(names[pick]);`

steps.title: Name what you changed
steps.instructions: At the top of `script.js`, under the title line, write one sentence as a `//` comment saying what your rule is and what the game would sound like without it.
hints: A sound rule is something the game decides. "Every catch in a row is a step higher" is a rule; "I changed a number" is not.

requirements.title: You added one sound rule
requirements.description: Any one challenge turns this green: a streak that sets the chime's rate, a pan that follows something in the game (not a fixed number), or slices of one file (or a sound rule of your own, such as a fade, or a rate that follows the score). Help: 6.11.5 (Lab: A sound that varies)
requirements.hint: Challenge 1 is one new variable and three lines: streak += 1; chime.rate = 1 + streak * 0.1; and streak = 0; for a miss.

requirements.title: You wrote your sentence
requirements.description: A // comment of at least four words at the top of the file, above the first line of code, saying what your rule is and what the game would sound like without it. Any wording works; only the title line already at the top does not count, with or without its lesson number. Help: this lab's step 2
requirements.hint: Under the title line: // then a sentence, such as: Each catch in a row is a step higher, so a streak sounds like a climb.
